name: גבול של מנה רציונלית באינסוף – דרגת המכנה גדולה באחת (באנגלית)
questiontext:
A rational function is a quotient of two polynomials. Evaluate the following limit of a rational function:

\( \displaystyle \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}}{\left(\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}\right)} = \) [[input:ans1]]
[[validation:ans1]]

If the limit does not exist, enter the value 1111 as your answer.
generalfeedback:
Outline: Keep only the highest powers; to justify it, divide the numerator and the denominator by the highest power.
Step 1 — The highest powers

The limit of the function

\[ \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}}{\left(\frac{{CT:2}}{{CT:3}}\right)}. \]

is the same as the limit found by keeping only the highest power terms in the numerator and the denominator. Hence resulting in a limit of {{CT:4}}.

Step 2 — Dividing by the highest power

The limit of the function can be found by dividing the numerator and denominator by {{CT:5}}.

The function can thus be expressed as

\[ \lim_{{{CT:0}} \rightarrow {{CT:1}}}{\left(\frac{{CT:6}}{{CT:7}}\right)}. \]

As {{CT:8}} tends to {{CT:9}}, all terms apart from the constant tend to zero.

Hence the limit is

\[ {{CT:10}} \]
